display_title: Integrated multi-omics analysis revealed the molecular networks and potential targets of cellular senescence in Alzheimer’s disease
summary: Separate blood and brain expression screens and cis-QTL analyses prioritized senescence-related Alzheimer’s disease candidates. The authors highlighted five blood-expression genes and two brain-expression genes. CDKN2B and ITGAV expression also rose in an amyloid-β-exposed PC12 cell comparison. The source reports two different denominators under the same FinnGen R9 label, so the genetic estimates are attributed to their specific figures and tables.
research_question: Which senescence-related genes show convergent expression and genetic-association signals in Alzheimer’s disease, and how far do the accompanying PC12 expression experiments support those candidates?
author_summary: The study integrates public blood and postmortem cortex transcriptomics, summary-level genetic associations, colocalization and a focused PC12 expression experiment. CENPW, SLFN12 and CDKN2B met the paper’s PPH4 > 0.5 colocalization threshold in their expression analyses, and SLFN12 also showed instrument heterogeneity. CDKN2B and ITGAV were followed up in the cell model. Conflicting FinnGen denominators and proposed mediation annotations are identified at their original source locations.

study_profile.study_design: Retrospective public transcriptomic screening with cis-eQTL/cis-mQTL two-sample Mendelian randomization, colocalization and a PC12 expression experiment.
study_profile.evidence_type: Human observational expression data, summary-level genetic prioritization and nonclinical cellular expression measurements.
study_profile.population: Public blood and postmortem prefrontal cortex AD/control datasets; predominantly European-ancestry QTL and FinnGen outcome resources; PC12 rat pheochromocytoma-derived cells for the laboratory comparison.
study_profile.primary_endpoint: Association of genetically instrumented gene expression or methylation with the AD GWAS outcome.
study_profile.secondary_endpoint: Senescence-related expression screening, colocalization, and CDKN2B/ITGAV mRNA and protein expression after Aβ1-42 exposure.
data_modalities: Bayesian colocalization and instrument heterogeneity assessment
PC12 qPCR and Western-blot expression measurements

key_findings.context: Candidate expression changes were aligned with the labelled CellAge signature. A GSVA difference score compares the up- and down-regulated signature sets. Figure S1 shows the blood comparisons in GSE63060 and GSE63061.

what_this_adds: Tissue-specific target prioritization that relates a labelled senescence signature to human blood and postmortem brain expression changes.
Gene-level comparisons of cis-QTL estimates, likelihood of colocalization and instrument heterogeneity.
Cellular follow-up for two brain candidates, measuring expression under a specified amyloid-β exposure.

supports: Reported case-control expression patterns in the named blood and brain datasets.
Source-attributed estimates for the highlighted eQTL and methylation candidates.
CDKN2B and ITGAV expression observations from the specified PC12 model.
does_not_establish: Exact identity of the GWAS run input or complete EXOSC9/SLFN12 mediation chains.
Prospective diagnostic performance, human treatment benefit or target-specific functional rescue.

qa.question: How do the five blood and two brain candidates relate to the eQTL test tables?
qa.answer: Table S1 has 94 tested rows and 13 adjusted P values below 0.05. Table S4 has 170 tested rows and four below 0.05. The Results report 179 brain genes after instrument selection and do not explain the difference from the table. The article highlights the five blood and two brain expression candidates with concordant directions.
qa.source_locator: supplementary_table_ddae189.xlsx: Supplementary Tables 1, 4 and 9; main Figures 2C and 4C.

qa.question: Which blood genes are highlighted?
qa.answer: Figure 2C reports ORs below one for CENPW, EXOSC9 and HSPB11, and above one for SLC44A2 and SLFN12. CENPW (PPH4 0.554) and SLFN12 (0.876) cross the study cutoff. SLFN12 also shows significant IVW heterogeneity (Table S2, Q P=4.29×10⁻⁵).
qa.source_locator: Publisher advance-article PDF p. 2 (Integration analysis from blood), p. 4 Figure 2C-I; supplementary_table_ddae189.xlsx, Supplementary Table 1 rows 15, 42, 49, 83 and 93 and Supplementary Table 2 rows 3-11; Table 9 supplies the expression-direction categories.

qa.question: How do CDKN2B and ITGAV differ genetically?
qa.answer: Reported ORs are 1.28 for CDKN2B and 1.09 for ITGAV. CDKN2B uses the rs490005 Wald ratio and has PPH4 0.607. ITGAV uses a five-SNP IVW model and has PPH4 0.452. The latter is below the study’s colocalization cutoff of 0.5.
qa.source_locator: Publisher advance-article PDF p. 5 (Integration analysis from brain), p. 7 Figure 4C; supplementary_table_ddae189.xlsx, Supplementary Table 4 rows 22 and 71 and Supplementary Table 5 rows 3-4; Table 9 supplies the expression-direction categories.

qa.question: How were the gene expression MR and colocalization estimates produced?
qa.answer: The Methods specify TwoSampleMR, a Wald ratio for one instrument and inverse-variance weighting for multiple instruments, plus coloc for region-level colocalization. The instrument criteria include P < 5×10⁻⁶ and LD clumping at r² < 0.1. The SMR resource provides QTL data.
qa.source_locator: Publisher PDF p. 9, Mendelian randomization analysis and Colocalization analysis; p. 10, Data availability; Table S10.

qa.question: What supports the methylation analysis, and where do the annotations disagree?
qa.answer: The reported methylation screens contain 18 blood probes across seven genes and 15 brain probes across six. The EXOSC9 probe identity and EXOSC9/SLFN12 expression-to-AD coefficients differ across Figures 1, 2C and 3C–D, Table 1, Table S1 and Figure S3. These discrepancies limit mechanistic interpretation of the proposed mediation paths.
qa.source_locator: Publisher advance-article PDF pp. 2 and 5 (blood/brain cis-mQTL analyses), p. 5 Table 1, pp. 6-7 Figures 3B and 4D; supplementary_table_ddae189.xlsx, Supplementary Tables 3 and 6; supplementary_figure_ddae189.docx, Figures S2-S4. Figures 1 and 3C-D contain unresolved mediation annotations.

qa.question: Which cell model was used to examine CDKN2B and ITGAV?
qa.answer: The Methods and Figure 4 identify rat-derived PC12 cells treated with 7 μM Aβ1–42 for 12 hours. The source’s reference to AD neurons in the Results does not identify another human cell experiment.
qa.source_locator: Publisher advance-article PDF p. 5 (Validation of the target genes expression), p. 7 Figure 4E-G, p. 9 (PC12 cell culture; qPCR; Western blot); supplementary_table_ddae189.xlsx, Supplementary Table 7 rows 2-12 and Supplementary Table 8 rows 2-26; supplementary_figure_ddae189.docx, Figures S5-S6.

qa.question: What changed in the PC12 expression comparison?
qa.answer: CDKN2B and ITGAV mRNA and protein signals were higher after Aβ1–42 exposure. The qPCR table records four measurements per group and target. The protein sheet records three labelled measurements per group. The biological independence of those measurements is unspecified. Figure 4F and Table S7 disagree on the ITGAV qPCR fold scale.
qa.source_locator: Publisher advance-article PDF p. 5 (Validation of the target genes expression), p. 7 Figure 4E-G, p. 9 (PC12 cell culture; qPCR; Western blot); supplementary_table_ddae189.xlsx, Supplementary Table 7 rows 2-12 and Supplementary Table 8 rows 2-26; supplementary_figure_ddae189.docx, Figures S5-S6.

qa.question: Which denominator is documented for the FinnGen AD outcome?
qa.answer: Methods and Table S10 give 9,301 cases and 367,976 controls. STROBE-MR item 4d gives 7,759 and 334,740 under the same R9 label. Official R9 Risteys lists 9,301 cases. It does not identify the file analyzed in the paper.
qa.source_locator: Publisher advance-article PDF p. 8, GWAS data for Alzheimer’s disease; Supplementary Table S10, FinnGen AD outcome row; supplementary_materials_ddae189.docx, STROBE-MR item 4d; FinnGen R9 Risteys endpoint G6_ALZHEIMER.

qa.question: How can these results inform Alzheimer’s disease research?
qa.answer: They provide tissue-specific candidates for studying relationships among senescence-associated expression, genetic associations and Aβ1–42 exposure. Report the relevant tissue and assay and distinguish the candidate association from clinical validation. Cite the original study for its results and use the linked figure or table for the specific observation.
qa.source_locator: Publisher PDF pp. 8-9, Discussion limitations and Materials and Methods; Figures 2 and 4.

limitations: MR interpretation depends on instrument relevance, independence and exclusion restriction, plus LD and ancestry assumptions. Colocalization and Cochran Q describe properties of the reported analyses.
The FinnGen denominator, certain mediation annotations and the ITGAV qPCR fold scale disagree across original sources. Each affected finding identifies the competing sources.

The PC12 assay measures expression. Supplementary Tables S7–S8 do not identify independent biological repeats; Supplementary Table S11 does not list the stated GAPDH reference primer and the printed CDKN2B reverse-primer sequence includes an ambiguous character.

related_papers.relationship: An independent neurodegeneration study combining transcriptomic analysis with genetic prioritization; its ALS/ABCA1 evidence does not validate AD candidate mechanisms.
